claim.pdf_says: Page 742 ends general rule 9 with only item a): "a) when identifier-1 references an intrinsic function, as though implicit-record-1 were a record description entry subordinate to the file description entry having the same class, category, usage, and length as the returned value of the intrinsic function, or". Items b) and c) are printed as separate, separately-indented list items at the TOP of page 743: "b) when identifier-1 does not reference an intrinsic function, ... having the same description as identifier-1, or" and "c) when literal-1 is specified, ... having the same class, category, usage, and length as literal-1."
claim.markdown_says: "   a) when identifier-1 references an intrinsic function, ... as the returned value of the intrinsic function, or b) when identifier-1 does not reference an intrinsic function, ... having the same description as identifier-1, or c) when literal-1 is specified, ... having the same class, category, usage, and length as literal-1." - all three items run together as ONE paragraph inside the page-742 slice; the page-743 slice begins at "NOTE 3", with no b) or c) items.
claim.why_it_matters: Three distinct sub-items of REWRITE general rule 9 are collapsed into a single run-on paragraph and two of them are attributed to the wrong page. The list structure is what makes "General rule 9b" and "General rule 9c" citable, and the run-on form makes the item boundaries invisible to any tooling or reader that splits on list markers. The wording itself is intact, so this is structural rather than a loss of normative text.

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED as a content discrepancy. Both of the claim's factual observations are ACCURATE, but the difference is newline placement plus page-slice attribution for a list that spans a page break - the explicitly excluded 'page-break furniture / line wrapping / formatting' class - and it changes no meaning and loses no text.

WHAT THE PDF PRINTS (rendered at 300 dpi). E:/Temp/specrecon/v742/spec_p742.png (printed folio 712) ends 14.9.34.3 general rule 9 with the lead-in 'where implicit-record-1 refers to the record area for file-name-1 and is treated:' followed by exactly ONE lettered item, 'a) when identifier-1 references an intrinsic function, ... as the returned value of the intrinsic function, or', and then nothing but the '712  (c)ISO/IEC 2023' folio and the license footer. E:/Temp/specrecon/v743/spec_p743.png (printed folio 713) opens directly under the running head with 'b) when identifier-1 does not reference an intrinsic function, ...' and 'c) when literal-1 is specified, ...' as two separately hanging-indented items, then NOTE 3. So the claim's description of the PDF is correct.

WHAT THE MARKDOWN HOLDS. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 30210 is a single 674-character line carrying all three items joined by spaces; the page-743 anchor follows at line 30212 and that slice does begin at NOTE 3. So the claim's description of the markdown is also correct.

WHY IT IS NOT A CONTENT DISCREPANCY.
(1) NOTHING IS MISSING, ALTERED, DUPLICATED OR REORDERED. The identical a)/b)/c) construction appears a second time in the spec for the WRITE statement at specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 33141-33145, where the transcription DOES render it as three separate list items. I compared the two mechanically after normalizing U+2011 to ASCII hyphen and collapsing whitespace: both are the SAME 97-token stream, identical element for element. The run-on paragraph therefore carries the complete normative text of all three items, in the correct order, with no loss.
(2) THE ITEM MARKERS SURVIVE. I looked at the characters myself: in line 30210 the marker 'a)' is at offset 3, 'b)' at offset 263 and 'c)' at offset 476, each preceded by a space and followed by the item's own text. The boundaries between items are NOT invisible - they are printed in the running text exactly as ISO letters them. A reader searching 'b) when identifier-1 does not reference' finds general rule 9b in the markdown. The claim's 'invisible to any tooling or reader that splits on list markers' overstates it: it is false for a reader, and true only for a hypothetical consumer that splits on LINE-LEADING markers, which is an assumption about a downstream tool rather than a difference between the PDF and its transcription.
(3) THE PAGE ATTRIBUTION IS THE PAGE-BREAK ARTIFACT ITSELF, AND IS LOSSLESS. Items b) and c) sit before the page-743 anchor instead of after it, but they are not duplicated into the 743 slice and nothing from 743 is dropped - that slice correctly begins at NOTE 3 and continues through general rules 10, 11 and 12, all of which I checked line by line against the render. Reading order across the boundary is unchanged. A forensic detail confirms the mechanism: item a) is transcribed with ASCII hyphens while items b) and c) use U+2011 non-breaking hyphens (8 of them in the line), the same encoding used throughout the page-743 slice. b) and c) were transcribed as part of page 743's text run and then merged forward by the page splitter - that is page-break furniture by definition.

CALIBRATION AGAINST THIS LEDGER. This matches the class already rejected in verify-p163-misplaced-content-1 ('newline placement inside a display block that spans a page break') and verify-p243-misplaced-content-4 ('pure line-breaking / page-boundary furniture with zero content loss'). It is materially WEAKER than verify-p154-misplaced-content-0, which was accepted (real=true) because there a structural LABEL, 'Format 3 (reference-modification):', was glued onto the tail of a preceding skeleton line and thereby stopped being distinguishable as a format heading. Here no label is absorbed or disguised; the letters a), b) and c) remain intact, spaced, and in sequence.

RESIDUE WORTH ONE LINE, NOT A FINDING. The transcription is internally inconsistent - the same passage is split correctly at lines 33141-33145 and run together at line 30210. That is a cosmetic formatting inconsistency in the transcription, fixable at zero risk by inserting two blank lines, but it is not a discrepancy between the PDF and the markdown's content and must not be counted as one.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. Both quotations are accurate, but every word of REWRITE general rule 9 items a), b) and c) is present in the markdown, verbatim, in order, with the a)/b)/c) markers intact at offsets 3, 263 and 476 of specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 30210 - token-identical (97 tokens) to the same passage rendered correctly as three separate items for the WRITE statement at lines 33141-33145. The only differences are that the blank lines between the items were not emitted, and that items b) and c), which print at the top of PDF page 743, were merged forward into the page-742 slice by the page splitter (evidenced by their U+2011 non-breaking hyphens, page 743's encoding, versus item a)'s ASCII hyphens). Nothing is lost, duplicated or reordered, the page-743 slice correctly resumes at NOTE 3, and no meaning changes. This is line-wrapping plus page-break furniture, the excluded class. The residual cosmetic issue - the transcription splits this same list correctly elsewhere but not here - is a formatting inconsistency, not a reconciliation finding.
